input: Price out a bathroom tile replacement project

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Tiling just the floor vs. floor plus walls vs. a full shower surround changes material quantities and labour costs dramatically.
Bathroom size (square footage) is the primary driver of how much tile and labour is needed, directly setting the cost baseline.
Whether the user plans to DIY or hire a professional determines whether to price labour at all and how to source quotes.
Tile material and style (ceramic, porcelain, natural stone, large-format, mosaic) have wildly different per-unit costs and installation complexity.
A hard budget ceiling changes which options are worth pricing and whether a phased or partial replacement is more realistic.
Whether existing tile needs to be demoed and subfloor inspected/repaired adds significant cost and timeline that must be factored in.
Knowing whether the user needs a rough ballpark, a detailed line-item estimate, or actual contractor quotes determines how deep the research needs to go.

gold.taskTitle: Price out a bathroom tile replacement project
gold.taskDescription: Gather accurate cost estimates for replacing the tile in a bathroom, covering materials, labour, and any related work.

questions.title: Which surfaces are you retiling — floor, walls, shower, or all?
questions.description: Identify the exact surfaces included in the project scope to calculate accurate material quantities and labour scope.

questions.title: What is the approximate square footage of the bathroom?
questions.description: Capture the size of the space to establish the primary cost driver for both tile materials and installation labour.

questions.title: Are you hiring a contractor or planning to do it yourself?
questions.description: Determine whether labour costs need to be priced out and whether the research involves getting trade quotes.

questions.title: What tile material or style are you leaning toward?
questions.description: Identify the tile type (ceramic, porcelain, natural stone, mosaic, etc.) since this is one of the biggest variables in per-square-foot cost.

questions.title: Do you have a maximum budget in mind for this project?
questions.description: Establish any hard financial ceiling so the pricing research can focus on realistic options and flag if the scope needs to be adjusted.

questions.title: Does the existing tile need to be removed before new tile is installed?
questions.description: Determine whether demolition, disposal, and potential subfloor repair costs need to be included in the estimate.

questions.title: Do you need a rough ballpark or a detailed, itemised cost breakdown?
questions.description: Clarify the required depth of the estimate so the plan targets the right level of research — quick ranges vs. line-item contractor-ready figures.
